newsitem.title: UK: BOE says money market changes in line with EMU.
newsitem.headline: BOE says money market changes in line with EMU.

text.p: The Bank of England said the changes in money market operations it announced today were consistent with preparations for a single European currency.

"The changes to be implemented from March 3 are consistent with the direction and spirit of the preparatory work for monetary union published by the European Monetary Institute in January," it said it a paper entitled "Reform of the Bank of England's operations in the sterling money markets."
The main changes will be the use of gilt repos in daily money market operations from March 3 and the broadening of the range of counterparties with which the Bank will deal.

"The plans being drawn up for monetary operations by the future European Central Bank are relevant to any further development of the Bank's operations, whether or not the United Kingdom participates in monetary union," the Bank said.
Executive director Ian Plenderleith said the changes were not consciously intended to be consistent with moves towards a single currency but were part of a general international trend.
A number of central banks in Europe and elsewhere had been adapting their market operations to take account of changes, he told Reuters Financial Television.

"They are all tending to converge on the same model -- relatively frequent operations in order to be able to conduct fine-tuning when necessary, using prime, liquid open-market instruments," Plenderleith said
"In that sense, yes, we're, I think, converging on the international model but others have as well, including others adapting some features of our operations."

The Bank's report said the expanded range of counterparties with which it would be prepared to deal would include banks, building societies and securities firms supervised by "a competent authority in the European Economic Area."
